newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex calls for bids on $1 bln nitrogen plant.
newsitem.headline: Pemex calls for bids on $1 bln nitrogen plant.

text.p: Mexican state-owned oil corporation Pemex is preparing to receive bids to build and run the world's largest nitrogen plant in the Gulf of Mexico, according to documents obtained by Reuters.

Pemex's Exploration and Production (PEP) division, in its international tender number CPEP-S-IT-112-97-SV4, refers to a "contract to supply PEP with a daily average of 1.5 billion standard cubic feet."
July 25 is the deadline for interested companies to request details of the project, and August 5 for tendering technical bids. A date has yet to be fixed for announcing the winners of the bid.

"It should be borne in mind that the nitrogen plant to be built will be, by far the world's biggest," Pemex Director General Adrian Lajous recently said in the Gulf of Mexico port of Ciudad del Carmen.
The plant is to be located in the Cantarell field in the Campeche Sound.

Lajous added that nitogen produced in the new plant would be injected into the Cantarell oil fields to raise pressure there and help boost crude oil output to 1.223 billion barrels per day, up from a current 1.074 billion barrels per day.
Sources at construction companies told Reuters the contract would be worth close to $1 billion for the period between 1997 and the delivery date in the year 2001.
"We are aware of the project. We will enter with Fluor Daniel," a director at Mexican construction firm Empresas ICA said.
A source at another major Mexican building company, Bufete Industrial, also said the project would require investment of $1 billion. Bufete would also bid for the project, the source said.

Despite the scale of the project, Pemex has not given the plant the same level of publicity as that enjoyed by a call for bids due in August to modernize the Cadereyta refinery, which is estimated to be worth $1.2 billion.
